title: Chapter 194: So Painful! So Painful!
html:
Beyond the tape and newspaper, the office contained many clues about Xu Zhenzhen. A broken frame in one corner of the bookshelf held a photograph of a father and daughter with both faces obscured. The desk drawer contained the man’s will, which also named Xu Zhenzhen. Not a single clear image of her appeared anywhere, yet her name permeated the entire attraction.

Tian Teng Medical School based this attraction on a real case. Aren’t they afraid of summoning the real Xu Zhenzhen?Haunted Houses naturally accumulated negative energy. Shielded from sunlight, they provided ideal hiding places for spirits and ghosts. People say dreams reflect reality. Visitors call Xu Zhenzhen’s name here every day. What if she heard them?

Tian Teng Medical School had no idea what it had done. The designers recreated a real tragedy and scattered its authentic details as clues. Others might call the concept clever; Chen Ge considered it playing with fire.

There are ‘gods’ everywhere. Even if you don’t believe in them, you don’t need to go and actively taunt them.

For all his courage, Chen Ge never treated the unknown carelessly. That was why he prepared so thoroughly for every Trial Mission. He had completed more than half of Tian Teng Medical School, and the corridor ahead was growing brighter.

It’s time to leave.

Whether Xu Zhenzhen truly haunted the attraction, Chen Ge did not know. His objective remained simple: complete the challenge and leave. After another circuit of the room, he returned to the recorder. As he approached, he heard faint, muffled sobbing from within.

Is the ghost inside the tape emerging?Chen Ge stepped back, closed one hand around the ballpoint pen in his pocket, and lightly nudged the “corpse” on the desk. If something went wrong, he would have no time to protect the actor.

To his surprise, the slightest touch sent the man toppling sideways onto the floor.

What happened? Is it Xu Zhenzhen?He had encountered enough ghosts to recognize the possible signs of a real manifestation. Am I truly this lucky? I visit someone else’s Haunted House and still find a ghost.

Remembering his Specter’s Favored title, Chen Ge began to panic. He hurried to help the fallen man before it was too late. An actor dies while playing dead? What kind of headline would that make?

As Chen Ge crouched to seize the man’s hand, a human head shot from beneath the desk. The actor’s body had concealed the mechanism. At such close range, Chen Ge had no time to dodge. The head struck his chest, sending his heart racing for several seconds.

Chen Ge looked at the mannequin head in his arms and the ‘dead body’ on the ground, and it dawned on him. “Brother, are you trying to get revenge for humiliating you at the nursery?”

When the “corpse” lay across the desk, his face had been hidden. Now Chen Ge recognized the actor from beneath the crib; the man had not even changed his makeup, merely smeared more fake blood over it. Chen Ge checked beneath his nose, confirmed he was breathing, and stood. It was time to leave.

He pressed the recorder’s stop button, then pressed it again. The tape continued turning. None of the other controls responded either. It won’t stop?

He could not abandon the tape here, yet taking the recorder would be theft. As he worked the controls, the faint sobbing grew louder, accompanied by a muffled electrical hum.

Chen Ge tried to remember the introduction to the tapes. About one second later, a voice appeared on the recording. It could have been male or female, and it only appeared for mere seconds.

Someone is talking? What is he trying to say?

This was Chen Ge’s first communication with the tape. He dared not dismiss it; the black phone itself had awarded him this ghost. He listened patiently until the voice returned.

“Pain…” Mixed within white noise, the voice sounded unreal. As the tape continued to play, the voice became clearer.

It’s a man’s voice, and it sounds young.

As Chen Ge concentrated on the tape, the recorder’s play button suddenly depressed farther. He glanced at the “corpse” on the floor. The actor had heard the strange sounds too and secretly pressed a miniature remote in his pocket. It was already too late. The Baleful Specter within the cassette had awakened; no control could stop it now.

“So painful…”

The voice grew louder, as though the Baleful Specter was gradually losing control. Chen Ge could think of only one solution: leave with the entire recorder.

After several failed attempts to stop it, the “corpse” on the floor finally spoke. “What’s happening?”

He sat up with the fake blood flowing down his face.

“Is something wrong with your equipment?” Chen Ge could hardly admit that he had inserted a Baleful Specter into their recorder and could no longer remove it.

“I suppose so.” Equally uncertain, the actor reached toward it. Before his fingers made contact, a bloodcurdling scream erupted from the speaker.

” So painful!”

The actor shivered, and he pulled back his hand like he had been shocked.

“Why are you frightened? Isn’t this part of your Haunted House?” Chen Ge positioned himself before the recorder to prevent an accident.

“I was present when we recorded it. That voice wasn’t there!” the “corpse” insisted. He pulled out his phone and messaged the staff chat: “Who tampered with the tape in the director’s office?”

There was no answer, but in this short period, the voice coming from the recorder turned mad. It was filled with endless hate and resentment.

” So painful! So f*cking painful!”

The voice sounded as though real knives were punching holes through its body, each desperate effort to stanch one wound followed by another opening elsewhere. The actor trembled. This time, his fear was genuine.

“Your Haunted House sure is courageous to use an actual incident to design your set. Weren’t you afraid that the spirit might return to haunt you?”

Chen Ge purposely lowered his voice as he stared at the actor.

“They say you should never repeat a dead person’s name carelessly, spoken or written. Otherwise, something terrible may answer.”

“Stop!” the actor yelped. He reported everything happening in the office to the staff chat, then forced confidence into his voice. “It’s only a technical malfunction. Everything will be fine.”

The moment he finished, footsteps pounded outside. The “pregnant ghost” from the nursery rushed in, terror written across her face.

She was holding a piece of paper in her hand, and she was gasping for air.

“Ah Rui? Why are you here?” the actor asked nervously. He was already panicking, and it only heightened when he saw the female actor.

“Something appeared on the note. I saw it by accident.” She thrust the paper toward him. “She’s back!”
